Riemann Sum Visualizer

See Riemann sums come alive: canvas bar visualization for left, right, midpoint and trapezoidal sums of any function over [a, b], all four estimates compared.

📖 How to use

  1. Type f(x), the limits a and b, and the number of rectangles n.
  2. Pick left, right, midpoint or trapezoid to choose which rectangles the canvas draws.
  3. Press Draw to render the curve with the approximating bars.
  4. Compare all four sums in the stat cards — watch them converge as you raise n.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between the four sums?

Left uses f at each subinterval's left end, right uses the right end, midpoint uses the center, and trapezoid averages left and right (drawing trapezoids instead of rectangles).

Why do the sums disagree for small n?

Each method samples the function at different points, so on a sloped curve left under- or over-estimates. As n grows, all four converge to the true integral.

What functions can I type?

Polynomials (x^2), sin, cos, tan, exp, ln, sqrt, abs, pi, e, with + − * / ^ and parentheses.
